Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.persistence.adapter

Class ConversationRepositoryAdapter

java.lang.Object
com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.persistence.adapter.ConversationRepositoryAdapter
All Implemented Interfaces:
ConversationRepository
@Component public class ConversationRepositoryAdapter extends Object implements ConversationRepository
Spring Data JPA-backed adapter for the ConversationRepository domain port (US-10-003).

Owner-scoped reads dispatch on the sealed ConversationOwner type to one of two query pairs in ConversationJpaRepository — keyset pagination over the (created_at desc, id desc) composite, mirroring AgentRepositoryAdapter.

Owner-scoped writes resolve exactly one parent reference (UserJpa via JpaRepository.getReferenceById(ID) or ApiKeyJpa via JpaRepository.getReferenceById(ID)) so neither write triggers an extra SELECT just to satisfy the association.

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public Page<Conversation> listByOwner(ConversationOwner owner, Optional<AgentId> agentFilter, Cursor cursor, int pageSize)
      Description copied from interface: ConversationRepository
      Returns one page of conversations owned by owner, ordered newest-first ((createdAt, id) DESC), optionally narrowed to a single agent via agentFilter. The adapter switches exhaustively on the sealed ConversationOwner to dispatch the right where clause against the V005 XOR columns (owner_user_id / owner_client_id).

    • deleteById

      @Transactional public void deleteById(ConversationId id)
      Description copied from interface: ConversationRepository
      Hard-deletes the conversation identified by id. Messages cascade via the V001 FK chain (messages.conversation_id … on delete cascade). A non-existent id is a silent no-op at this layer; the use case is responsible for surfacing 404.
      Specified by:
      deleteById in interface ConversationRepository

    • appendMessage

      @Transactional public Message appendMessage(Message message)
      Description copied from interface: ConversationRepository
      Appends a Message to its parent conversation. Does NOT bump the parent's MessageCount — the caller is responsible for performing the read-modify-write of Conversation.incrementMessageCount(java.time.OffsetDateTime) and ConversationRepository.save(Conversation) in the same transactional boundary (REQ-STR-002 persistence ordering).
      Specified by:
      appendMessage in interface ConversationRepository

    • listMessages

      Description copied from interface: ConversationRepository
      Returns one page of messages of conversationId in chronological ascending order ((createdAt, id) ASC) — opposite of the conversations list. Backs GET /conversations/{conversationId}/messages (US-10-010).

    • findLastN

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public List<Message> findLastN(ConversationId conversationId, int n)
      Description copied from interface: ConversationRepository
      Returns the last n messages of conversationId in chronological ascending order. Backs EPIC-11's memory-window assembly (REQ-AGT-005). Implementations SHOULD query in descending order with LIMIT n and reverse before returning, so the database can use the (conversation_id, created_at, id) index.
      Specified by:
      findLastN in interface ConversationRepository
